summary: Dimension-graded Chow groups extend the native locally finite cycle carrier. Their operations feed refined intersection and Chern theory, source-scoped projective Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch, surface Riemann–Roch and Hodge index, the graph-of-Frobenius Weil bound, DM-stack comparisons and positive-characteristic semiampleness. Arithmetic surface pairings are imported from StableReduction Layer 4.

nodes.title: Dimension functions
nodes.statement: Fix a locally Noetherian universally catenary base S with an integer dimension function δS. For X locally of finite type over S set δX(x)=δS(f(x))+trdeg(κ(x)/κ(f(x))). Along an immediate specialization the value falls by one. Dimension grades always use this induced function, including on open subschemes; they are not silently replaced by Krull dimension of the open scheme.
hypotheses: Situation 42.7.1: S locally Noetherian and universally catenary, with a dimension function; X locally of finite type over S.
proofSteps: Use the dimension-function specialization rule and the transcendence-degree tower formula. Restriction to opens retains the values of the ambient function.
acceptance: Shifting by 2 and then by −1 shifts the original value by 1.
For a DVR base with δ(closed)=0 the generic value is 1; the inherited grade on its generic open is 1 even though that open has Krull dimension 0.
Zero shift preserves the entire dimension function.

sources.match: Supplies the ambient base and induced dimension function; the one-dimensional base example fixes the generic-point shift.

proofSteps: Take generic points of d-dimensional components, attach the lengths of their Artinian local rings and assemble the native locally finite support function.

Spec ℚ has zero-dimensional fundamental coefficient 1.

nodes.title: Rational equivalence
nodes.statement: Rat_d(X)⊂Z_d(X) consists of sums of principal boundary cycles from a locally finite family of integral closed (d+1)-dimensional W⊂X with a rational unit on each W. Local finiteness refers to the family of closed supports. In the Noetherian quasi-compact case this is the subgroup generated by finite principal sums; for a non-quasi-compact scheme finite generation alone is too small.
hypotheses: Situation 42.7.1; local finiteness of the closed family in each relation.
proofSteps: Each locally finite family gives a native locally finite coefficient sum. Unions of two such families and inversion make the set an additive subgroup. On a quasi-compact Noetherian scheme the family is finite.
acceptance: On P¹, [0]−[∞] is a rational relation.
The zero cycle is a relation, with the empty family.
A unit point on Spec ℚ is not a relation: there are no one-dimensional closed supports.

nodes.title: Proper pushforward preserves rational equivalence
nodes.statement: For a proper S-morphism f:X→Y, the existing dimension-weighted native cycle map carries Rat_d(X) into Rat_d(Y). For W generically finite over its image use the norm of a rational unit; if its image loses one dimension use degree zero of a principal divisor on the proper generic curve; greater dimension loss gives zero.
hypotheses: f proper over S; the same base induces δX and δY.
proofSteps: Separate the image dimensions. Apply the order-of-norm identity in the equal-dimensional case, the proper-curve principal-degree identity in relative dimension one, and the native weight cutoff for all remaining cases. Properness keeps images of locally finite closed families locally finite.
acceptance: For a finite map of integral curves the norm identity holds with inseparable residue degrees as well as separable ones.

sources.match: Provides the norm and generic-curve cases in the proper descent proof.

hypotheses: f proper over S; compatible induced dimension functions.
proofSteps: Homogeneity is preserved by the native weight match. Its pointwise linearity gives an additive homomorphism. Apply proper-relations to descend the quotient.
acceptance: A finite map with residue extension degree 2 sends a unit point to twice the image point.
A positive-dimensional integral support contracted to a lower-dimensional image pushes to zero.

nodes.title: Flat pullback
nodes.statement: For a flat S-map f:X→Y locally of finite type of constant relative dimension r, pull back a generator [W] to the (d+r)-dimensional fundamental cycle of X×Y W, with its generic lengths. This extends to locally finite cycles and descends to f*:CH_d(Y)→CH_(d+r)(X). A flat map with fibres of mixed dimension does not have this single graded pullback.
hypotheses: f flat and locally of finite type, with every nonempty fibre pure of the same dimension r≥0.
proofSteps: Flatness preserves the generic support dimension and controls local finiteness. Generic lengths define the cycle pullback. The valuation and flat length calculation carries principal relations to principal relations.
acceptance: Relative dimension zero for the identity does not shift the grade.
Pulling back the unit point along Spec ℚ[ε]/ε²→Spec ℚ gives the doubled fundamental point, rather than its reduction.

nodes.statement: For a finite locally free S-morphism f:X→Y of constant rank n, f_*f*=n on CH_d(Y) in every grade, with the pure relative dimension zero pullback. Generic nonreduced lengths are part of n.

proofSteps: Check the fibre algebra length weighted by residue degrees is its vector-space rank n on every integral generator. Descend by the existing proper and flat relation compatibilities.

nodes.title: Localization for Chow homology
nodes.statement: For a closed immersion i:Z→X with complementary open j:U→X, CH_d(Z)→CH_d(X)→CH_d(U)→0 is exact, using restricted ambient dimensions. The closed pushforward need not be injective.
hypotheses: Closed/open complementary pair in Situation 42.7.1.
proofSteps: Restrict locally finite cycles to the open. Extend integral supports by closure and rational units by their function fields. The difference of two lifts is supported on Z, yielding the kernel description.

nodes.title: Affine bundle homotopy invariance
nodes.statement: For a vector bundle, or a Zariski locally trivial affine-space bundle, p:E→X of constant relative rank r, flat pullback p*:CH_d(X)→CH_(d+r)(E) is an additive isomorphism. This is not asserted for every flat morphism.
hypotheses: Zariski locally trivial affine-space bundle of constant rank r, over the same S.
proofSteps: Surjectivity is the separate affine-bundle-surjectivity target (42.32.1). For a geometric vector bundle compactify as P(E dual ⊕ O), with divisor at infinity P(E dual). Cartier Gysin/projection and uniqueness in the projective bundle formula show that the pullback is injective (42.36.3). This gives the isomorphism required by refined Gysin. Arbitrary Zariski locally trivial affine-space bundles need the higher-Chow localization input outlined in Remark 42.32.8; that larger injectivity argument is recorded as a gap, not obtained by elementary gluing.
acceptance: CH₀(A¹)=0 and CH₁(A¹)=ℤ over a field, so unshifted homotopy invariance is wrong.

nodes.title: First Chern class operators
nodes.statement: For an invertible sheaf L on X, c₁(L)∩−:CH_d(X;ℤ)→CH_(d−1)(X;ℤ) sends an integral support W to the divisor of a nonzero rational section of L|W, pushed to X. Different rational sections differ by a principal divisor. The operator, unlike intersection of arbitrary Weil divisors on a singular scheme, is defined on every X in Situation 42.7.1.
hypotheses: L is the existing invertible-sheaf object; the same dimension base as Chow.
proofSteps: Construct the rational-section divisor by local trivializations and glue the order coefficients. Principal boundaries remove the choice of rational section. The two-dimensional tame-boundary formula proves that this operation kills rational relations.
acceptance: c₁(O(1))∩[P¹] is the class of a single point.
c₁(O(2))∩[P¹] is twice a point, detecting the tensor convention.
The trivial bundle kills every Chow class in every grade.

nodes.title: Projective bundles and tautological quotients
nodes.statement: For a finite locally free O_X-module E of rank r, construct P_X(E)=Proj_X(Sym E) with the quotient convention, π:P(E)→X and the universal rank-one quotient π*E→O(1). proofSteps: Use the SF.0 relative Proj construction and its homogeneous standard opens to glue the quotient classifiers. Glue O(1) and the universal quotient from the degree-one generators; apply the same construction after base change.
acceptance: The projectivization of the zero module is the empty scheme.

nodes.title: Projective bundle formula
nodes.statement: For E of constant positive rank r, with ξ=c₁(O(1)), the map ⊕_(j=0)^(r−1) CH_(d−r+1+j)(X)→CH_d(P(E)), (a_j)↦Σ ξ^j∩π*a_j, is an isomorphism. Moreover π_*(ξ^s∩π*a)=0 for s<r−1 and equals a for s=r−1.
hypotheses: E finite locally free of constant rank r>0; π flat of relative dimension r−1 and proper.
proofSteps: The top-power push formula in Lemma 42.36.1, together with lower-power vanishing and the Chern projection formula, proves uniqueness of the coefficients. On a trivial bundle use the hyperplane complement and affine-bundle surjectivity, then localization. Noetherian induction and the same locally finite support argument give existence in general. Do not use vector-bundle injectivity here: it is a consequence of this formula.
acceptance: For the trivial rank-two bundle, the two summands have grades d−1 and d. For rank one there is just the identity summand.

sources.match: States the shifted direct-sum decomposition and the push coefficients with the fixed quotient convention.

nodes.title: Complete flag bundles
nodes.statement: Construct the complete quotient flag bundle q:F(E)→X by successive projectivizations of the kernels of the tautological quotient. Its pullback of E has a filtration with invertible quotients L₁,…,L_r. Pullback on every Chow group is injective, also after each base change; splitting means a filtration, not a claimed direct-sum isomorphism.
hypotheses: E finite locally free of constant rank r; successive projective kernels are finite locally free.
proofSteps: Iterate the projective quotient classifier and its locally split kernel. Projective bundle push coefficients produce a left inverse at each step; compose them to prove injectivity.
acceptance: For rank one the flag bundle is the base itself.
For a trivial rank-two bundle over a point the complete flag scheme is P¹.
A Chow class whose flag pullback is zero was already zero.

Set c₀=id and c_i=0 for i>r. They are central natural operations for proper pushforward, flat pullback and Cartier Gysin; X need not be smooth.

proofSteps: Use projective bundle uniqueness to solve the relation for its coefficients. The rank-one case is the section-divisor first Chern operator. Pull the projective relation through proper/flat/Cartier operations to prove compatibility; splitting proves integral centrality.
acceptance: Every positive Chern operator of the trivial rank-two bundle is zero.

nodes.title: Normal cones and normal bundles
nodes.statement: For a closed immersion i:Z→X with ideal I, the normal cone C_ZX is Spec_Z(⊕_(n≥0) I^n/I^(n+1)). Its zero section and projection are intrinsic. For a regular immersion of constant codimension c, I/I² is locally free of rank c and C_ZX is the normal vector bundle (I/I²)∨. Proj of this graded algebra is the projectivized cone, not the cone itself.
hypotheses: Closed immersion between locally Noetherian schemes; regularity and constant codimension only for the vector bundle identification.
proofSteps: Construct the graded normal algebra on affine charts and glue by relative Spec. The regular-sequence associated-graded calculation identifies it with Sym(I/I²).
acceptance: The normal cone of the origin in A¹ over ℚ is A¹, not P⁰.
The identity immersion has zero normal rank.
At the origin of V(xy) in A² the normal cone is V(xy), a reducible cone rather than a rank-one vector space.

nodes.title: Deformation to the normal cone
nodes.statement: For a closed immersion i:Z→X, the open deformation M_ZX is Bl_(Z×{0})(X×A¹) with the strict transform of X×{0} removed. Its parameter t is a nonzerodivisor, its special fibre is C_ZX, and its restriction over G_m is X×G_m. Over a field k the parameter map M_ZX→A¹_k is flat. Over a general dimension base only the Cartier parameter and fibre identities are asserted. In the P¹ blowup compactification the exceptional divisor is the projective completion of C_ZX with an added trivial direction. For regular i this is P(N_ZX∨⊕O_Z) in the quotient convention. Its intersection with the strict transform is the projectivized cone without that direction. The blowup is imported from existing StableReduction Layer 4.
hypotheses: Closed immersion in the common locally Noetherian dimension base; a field base for parameter flatness; regularity only for the normal-bundle identification.
proofSteps: Apply the imported blowup to I+(t). Its open affine algebra is O_X[t,I/t] inside O_X[t,t⁻¹]; setting t=0 gives the normal algebra and inverting t gives O_X[t,t⁻¹]. Multiplication by t is injective. Over a field, this subalgebra is torsion-free as a k[t]-module, hence flat over k[t].
acceptance: The empty centre has empty special fibre; its open normal deformation is X×G_m.
Deforming the origin of A¹ gives A² with coordinates t and x/t.
The special fibre for the origin of V(xy) is the reducible node, retaining both branches.

sources.match: The blowup construction and affine deformation algebra identify the two fibres.
The compactified blowup and open normal-cone chart supply the specialization geometry.

nodes.statement: Let F,G be nonzero homogeneous polynomials of positive degrees m,n on P² over an algebraically closed field. Sum the local scheme lengths only over isolated points of V(F)∩V(G). Thus ch₀=r, ch₁=c₁, ch₂=(c₁²−2c₂)/2. For coherent M in the smooth quasiprojective resolution scope, define ch(M) by the alternating character of a finite locally free resolution. These are finite characteristic polynomials with denominators, not integral classes or an unbounded exponential.

nodes.title: Bivariant Chow classes
nodes.statement: For an S-morphism f:X→Y and integer p, a bivariant class of degree p is a family c_g:CH_d(Y′)→CH_(d−p)(X×Y Y′), for every S-map g:Y′→Y and every d. It commutes with proper pushforward, flat pullback of constant pure relative dimension, and refined Cartier Gysin in the sense of Definition 42.33.1. Pointwise addition gives A^p(X→Y). Pullback of the test map gives restriction, and composition of the families gives A^p(X→Y)×A^q(Y→Z)→A^(p+q)(X→Z). Identity gives the degree-zero unit. For X=Y these form the operational graded ring; it is not asserted commutative on singular schemes.
hypotheses: Situation 42.7.1 and compatible induced dimensions on every Cartesian test diagram; the original Cartier immersion and pulled-back line carry the source zero-locus condition.
proofSteps: Use the native abelian groups CH_d and additive homomorphisms to form the dependent family group. Cut out the subgroup satisfying the three explicitly transported naturality equalities. Addition preserves them. Restriction and composition of families preserve each equality by the proper/flat/Cartier operation laws.
acceptance: The identity family is the degree-zero unit. Zero cap on every test is the zero bivariant class. On Spec k the operational degree-zero group is ℤ acting by multiplication, including the nonzero identity.

nodes.title: Integral-support detection of bivariant classes
nodes.statement: For c∈A^p(X→Y), the following are equivalent: c=0; for every integral S-scheme Y′→Y, c∩[Y′]=0; for each such Y′ there is a proper birational Y″→Y′ with Y″ integral and c∩[Y″]=0. Equality of two classes follows by applying this criterion to their difference.
hypotheses: Situation 42.7.1; all test maps and dimensions induced from its fixed base; the modification is proper birational, not an arbitrary proper cover.
proofSteps: For any locally finite cycle take the coproduct of its integral closed supports. Its map to the test scheme is proper because the supports are locally finite. Proper naturality reduces cap to the integral fundamental classes. A proper birational modification pushes its fundamental class to the original one, proving the third criterion. This includes non-quasi-compact tests; finite-support generation alone is insufficient.
acceptance: Equality of refined classes can be checked after blowing up each integral test to make the two pulled-back centres Cartier, as in 42.54.8.

sources.match: Gives precisely the three equivalent vanishing tests and the locally finite coproduct proof.
